Pascal's Triangle, rows 1; 1 1; 1 2 1; 1 3 3 1; 1 4 6 4 1; 1 5 10 10 5 1. Each number is the sum of the two numbers diagonally above; if there is no second number, think of it as 0.
A. Write the numbers in the next three rows. (1 6 15 20 15 6 1; 1 7 21 35 35 21 7 1; 1 8 28 56 70 56 28 8 1)
B. Look for Relationships: What other patterns do you see? (The numbers one from the left move up by 1 in each row.)
C. Find the sum of the numbers in each row of the triangle. Write a formula for the sum of the numbers in the nth row. (1, 2, 4, 8, ..., 256; 2^n)
What do you notice about the triangle? → There's one more number in each row than in the row above it.
Compare the rows of the triangle. What similarities and differences can you find? → The first and last number of a row is always 1; in every other row the center number is repeated.
How does the sum of the numbers in one row in the triangle compare to that of the row above it? → The sum of a row is double the sum of the row above it.

Look at the sums of the numbers in the diagonals of rows 0 through 8. Then write out the numbers for row 9. What do you notice? Do you think this will always be true? → The sums of the diagonals are the same numbers as the next row with an additional 1 at the end. This is always true.
How could you determine the first two numbers of a row using your patterns? → Call the first row row 0. The first number is 1 and the second is the row number.
How do you know the last two numbers of a row? → The rows are symmetric, so the last two numbers are the first two in reverse order.
